topic: AiDex MCP Review 2026: Tree-sitter Code Search for Claude, Cursor, and Codex

competitors.title: AiDex README - Persistent Code Indexing for AI Assistants
key_points: Positions AiDex as a local-first MCP server with memory, semantic search, and live telemetry for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, and VS Code Copilot
Claims Tree-sitter-based parsing and persistent indexing let it replace repeated grep-based context gathering
Emphasizes zero-friction setup with auto-registration and cross-session persistence for tasks and notes

competitors.title: How I cut AI context usage by 50x with a Tree-sitter code index
key_points: Frames AiDex as an MCP server that turns code search into a single semantic query instead of repeated grep calls
Highlights Tree-sitter AST parsing, identifier-only indexing, and time-based filters as the core context-saving mechanics
Uses concrete token and latency claims to sell the product as a practical fix for token burn in agent workflows

competitors.title: CocoIndex Code - speed up Claude Code, Cursor & Codex
key_points: Competes directly on semantic code search with AST-aware Tree-sitter chunking and incremental re-indexing
Frames the value proposition as fewer tokens per turn and fewer retries for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex users
Shows the market is converging on MCP-based code context rather than simple text search

competitors.title: Tree-sitter Analyzer README - Cross-language-safe code intelligence MCP
key_points: Differentiates through structural analysis, call graphs, and blast-radius tools rather than just search
Targets Claude Code, Cursor, and other MCP clients with 100 percent local execution and TOON-compressed outputs
Leans into correctness claims for cross-language code understanding, which is a different promise than AiDex's memory-first pitch

competitors.title: code-review-graph - Local-first code intelligence for AI review
key_points: Builds a Tree-sitter-backed knowledge graph to restrict review context to the blast radius of a change
Explicitly targets AI code review efficiency with incremental updates and MCP integration
Competes with AiDex on token savings, but is more review- and dependency-analysis-oriented than memory-oriented

competitors.title: Building an Open-Source Alternative to Cursor with Code Context
key_points: Presents semantic code search as infrastructure for building your own Cursor-like workflow
Uses Tree-sitter AST parsing, incremental indexing, and MCP integration to serve Claude Code and other agents
Requires more moving parts than AiDex, which makes it a useful comparison point for setup complexity and control

stats.fact: AiDex positions itself as a persistent brain for AI coding agents with memory, semantic search, and live telemetry, and says it works with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, and VS Code Copilot
A DEV article on AiDex says a Tree-sitter-backed query can cut a 2000-plus token grep workflow down to about 50 tokens and a single tool call
CocoIndex Code claims Tree-sitter AST chunking, incremental re-indexing, and roughly 70 percent fewer tokens per turn for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
Tree-sitter Analyzer says it is a 100 percent local MCP server with 13 languages, 8 MCP tools, and TOON-compressed output for agent workflows
code-review-graph claims 6.8x fewer tokens on reviews and up to 49x fewer on daily coding tasks by using a persistent Tree-sitter knowledge graph
Milvus's Code Context article frames open-source semantic code search as the way to build a Cursor-like experience with Tree-sitter AST parsing, incremental indexing, and MCP support

angles: AiDex is not just another semantic search index: the strongest angle is persistent agent memory plus code context, which moves it closer to a durable assistant layer than a one-off retrieval tool

The real comparison is between search-first tools like AiDex and CocoIndex and structure-first tools like tree-sitter-analyzer and code-review-graph, so the article should separate semantic retrieval from blast-radius analysis

The article should answer whether AiDex is the simplest way to stop re-explaining the codebase to Claude, Cursor, and Codex, or whether heavier structural tools are better for large repos and review workflows
Setup friction matters: AiDex's auto-registration and client-agnostic MCP story is a stronger hook than more configurable but more involved stacks that require vector databases or extra services
The best audience is teams already living in MCP-compatible clients who want persistent recall and faster code search without adopting a full platform or enterprise analytics suite
A clear limitation to call out is that AiDex is optimized for search and memory, not for the deeper call-graph and cross-language correctness claims that structural analyzers make
